title: From This Mauve and Rose Dream...
text:
From this mauve and rose dream

that the river water dreams,

the sails of my ship

are blushing in the afternoon.


I come from distances.

I cross before the jetty.

A sailor's song

turns rosy in my heart...


Sunset. On the Plata.

I dream before the city.

I carry my sails raised,

sails of my solitude...


And with the day there go from me

-I do not know where they will go-

the lights of my joy.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the river dream, rose-colored sails, and departing lights of joy.

title: I Neither Understand Myself Nor Am Understood
text:
I neither understand myself nor am understood;

neither soul nor blood is of use to me;

what I see with my eyes

I would not wish on anyone.


Everything is strange to me myself,

even light, even air,

because I cannot manage to look at it,

nor do I know how to breathe it.


And if I look toward the shadow

where light comes undone,

I fear I too will come undone

and remain among the shadow,

confused forever

in that great mystery.
editorial_note: The translation preserves estrangement from self, light, air, and the dissolving shadow.

title: I Like to Walk Deserted Cities at Night
text:
I like to walk deserted cities at night,

when one's own steps are heard in the silence.

To feel oneself walking, alone, among what sleeps,

is to feel one is passing through an immense world.


Everything gains relief: an open window,

a light, a pause, a sigh, a shadow...

The streets are longer, time also grows.


I managed to live centuries by walking a few hours!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the nighttime walk as an expansion of city, silence, and time.

title: My Blood Came Away to Form Your Body...
text:
My blood came away to form your body.

My soul was divided to form your soul.

And there were nine moons, and it was all anguish

of days without rest and sleepless nights.


And it was at the hour of seeing you that I lost you without seeing you.

What color were your eyes, your hair, your shadow?

My heart, which is a cradle that keeps you in secret,

because it knows you existed and carried you in life,

will go on rocking you until the end of my hours.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the elegy for a child as blood, soul, unseen presence, and cradle.

title: I Rose as Far as Dream. I Was Going in Search...
text:
I rose as far as dream. I was going

        in search...



        "Life is a wounded deer

        to which arrows give wings."

        Góngora


I rose as far as dream. I was going in search

of not feeling the wound

        that burned.

The hard arrows of pain made

bloom in me the

        carnation of a new wound.


Running a race alongside the wind

and pursued by a lover's

        flame,

life is a wounded deer beyond remedy,

for the arrows give it

        poison and wings.
editorial_note: The translation keeps this longer variant's epigraph and staggered spacing while following the wound-and-wings image.
